content:
Buying camping gear in Nairobi starts with five essentials: a waterproof double-wall tent, a sleeping bag rated for the cold nights at altitude, an insulated sleeping pad, a gas stove with screw-on canisters, and a rechargeable headlamp. Quality thrifted gear from a specialist outdoor shop keeps the cost down without cutting corners.

Kenyan campsites can be warm at sunset and surprisingly cold by 3am, and the short rains bring heavy storms from October to December. This guide explains what camping gear in Nairobi to buy first, what to look for in each item, how new and thrifted gear compare, and where to buy it on Thika Road.

Quick Facts

  • Core kit: tent, sleeping bag, sleeping pad, stove and gas, headlamp, water
  • Night temperatures: campsites at 1,800-2,600 m can drop into single digits Celsius
  • Sleeping bag: comfort rating about 5°C to 10°C near Nairobi; 0°C to -10°C for Mt Kenya
  • Tent: double-wall with a full rainfly and taped seams for the rainy seasons
  • Gas: screw-on butane/propane canisters; not allowed on flights
  • Where to buy: Mountain Mall, 3rd Floor, Shop D39, Thika Road, Nairobi

What Camping Gear Do You Need for a Trip from Nairobi?

For a first camping trip from Nairobi you need shelter, warmth, light, cooking and water: a tent, sleeping bag, sleeping pad, headlamp, stove and fuel, and a way to carry and treat water. Everything else is comfort.

Popular weekend camping spots within a few hours of Nairobi include Kenya Wildlife Service parks such as Hell's Gate and Mt Longonot near Naivasha, forest campsites in the Aberdares and private sites in the Rift Valley. Most sit between about 1,800 m and 2,600 m, where clear nights can fall into single digits Celsius. That altitude, more than anything, decides what camping gear in Nairobi you should buy.

If you are buying camping gear in Nairobi for the first time, buy in this order: sleeping bag and pad first (cold nights ruin trips), then a headlamp, then a tent, then cooking kit. Some campsites and organised trips provide tents, so check before you buy one.

How Do You Choose a Tent for Kenyan Campsites?

Choose a double-wall, three-season dome tent with a full-length rainfly, taped seams and a bathtub floor. That design handles Kenya's afternoon downpours, wind on open ridges and the dust of the dry season.

What size tent should you buy?

A tent rated for one more person than will sleep in it gives you room for bags and boots inside, out of the rain. A two-person tent suits one camper with gear; a three-person tent suits a couple. If you plan to hike in to camp, keep the packed weight under about 2.5 kg per person.

Which waterproof rating is good enough?

Look for a fly rated at 1,500 mm hydrostatic head or more, and a higher rating on the floor, which takes the pressure of your body on wet ground. Taped seams matter as much as the number. With a thrifted tent, check before you buy that every pole, peg and zip is there and works.

Which Sleeping Bag Should You Buy for Camping in Kenya?

Buy a sleeping bag whose comfort rating is a few degrees below the coldest night you expect. For most camping near Nairobi, a comfort rating around 5°C to 10°C works; for Mt Kenya and the high Aberdares, look at 0°C to -10°C.

Sleeping bags tested to ISO 23537 show a comfort temperature and a lower limit temperature. Plan with the comfort figure, not the limit. When comparing sleeping bags as camping gear in Nairobi, remember that down bags are warmer for their weight and pack smaller, which suits mountain trips, while synthetic bags cope better with damp and are often cheaper. A mummy shape is warmest because there is less air to heat; our post on the mummy-shape down sleeping bag explains how that design works.

Why is a sleeping pad as important as the bag?

A sleeping pad matters because cold ground pulls heat from your body faster than cold air, and a sleeping bag's filling is crushed flat beneath you. Pads now carry an R-value under the ASTM F3340 standard: around 2 to 3 suits mild nights, and 4 or more suits cold ground at altitude.

When buying camping gear in Nairobi, check that each item suits Kenyan altitude and rain, that it works today, and that spares and fuel are easy to find locally. Use the checklist below in the shop.

Is thrifted camping gear in Nairobi worth buying?

Thrifted camping gear in Nairobi is usually worth buying, because tents, sleeping bags and stoves from good outdoor brands are built to last for years. Our stock is mainly quality thrifted (pre-owned) gear plus some new items, which makes reliable camping kit far more affordable than buying everything new. Inspect each item yourself using the checklist above.

What Cooking, Light and Water Gear Do You Need?

For cooking, light and water you need a compact gas stove, screw-on gas canisters, a pot and lighter, a bright headlamp, and enough bottles or a hydration bladder to carry 2 to 3 litres per person, plus a way to treat water.

Which camping gas should you buy?

Most lightweight backpacking stoves use screw-on (threaded) canisters filled with a butane and propane mix, which burns better in the cold than pure butane. If you are flying in, buy fuel locally along with your other camping gear in Nairobi, because airlines do not allow gas canisters. Our post on the Coleman C300 screw-on gas can covers one common option.

What makes a good camping headlamp?

A good camping headlamp gives at least 200 lumens for walking after dark, a red-light mode that does not dazzle your campmates, and a rechargeable battery or spares. A waterproof rechargeable headlamp keeps working through a stormy night and charges from a power bank. It is one of the cheapest pieces of camping gear in Nairobi that makes the biggest difference after dark.

How should you carry water?

Carry 2 to 3 litres per person for a day of walking, and more if the campsite has no tap. A 3L hydration backpack is handy for hikes from camp. Treat stream water with tablets, a filter or by boiling.

Camping Gear Buying Checklist

  • When shopping for camping gear in Nairobi, buy your sleep system (bag and pad) first.
  • Unzip every zip and test every buckle before you pay.
  • Check that your stove's thread fits the gas canisters you will actually use.
  • Ask whether the tent comes with all poles, pegs and guylines.
  • Try a backpack on with weight in it and the hip belt fastened.
  • Do a test night in the garden or a nearby campsite before a big trip.

How Do You Care for Camping Gear After a Trip?

Make your camping gear in Nairobi last by drying everything fully before storage, cleaning off mud and dust, and storing sleeping bags loose rather than compressed. Damp storage causes mould, smells and damaged waterproof coatings.

Pitch your tent or hang the fly on a balcony or washing line in Nairobi as soon as you get home, even if it looks dry. Brush ash and dust out of zips, because Rift Valley dust wears them quickly. Store down sleeping bags in a large cotton or mesh sack, and only use the small stuff sack on the trail. Remove gas canisters from stoves and keep them somewhere cool, out of direct sun.

Before each trip, check national park campsite rules and current fees with Kenya Wildlife Service. Keep food sealed inside the tent or car at night, because baboons and monkeys at some campsites are quick to raid open bags.

Frequently Asked Questions

Where can I buy camping gear in Nairobi?

You can buy camping gear in Nairobi at Hiking Outdoor Gear Hub, Mountain Mall, 3rd Floor, Shop D39, on Thika Road near Kasarani and Garden Estate. The shop opens Monday to Friday 8:30am to 6:00pm and Saturday 9:00am to 2:00pm, with Sunday by appointment. You can also order online and pay by M-Pesa or cash on delivery.

Is it cheaper to buy second-hand camping gear in Nairobi?

Second-hand camping gear in Nairobi is usually much cheaper than new gear of the same brand and quality, which is why thrifted tents, sleeping bags and stoves are popular with Kenyan campers. Good outdoor brands are built to last, so a well-kept pre-owned item can serve for years. Always check zips, seams, poles and fittings before paying.

What temperature sleeping bag do I need for camping in Kenya?

A sleeping bag with a comfort rating of about 5°C to 10°C suits most camping around Nairobi, Naivasha and the Rift Valley, where clear nights can drop into single digits. For the Aberdares and Mt Kenya, choose a bag with a comfort rating of 0°C to -10°C, and always pair it with an insulated sleeping pad.

Can I take camping gas on a plane to Kenya?

Camping gas canisters cannot be carried on passenger flights, in either cabin or checked luggage, because they are pressurised flammable gas. Visitors flying into Nairobi should bring an empty, clean stove and buy screw-on gas canisters locally. Check that the stove thread matches the canisters you can find in Nairobi before your trip.

Do I need a tent to camp in Kenyan national parks?

Kenyan national park campsites run by Kenya Wildlife Service generally provide a pitch and basic facilities, not tents, so you need to bring your own unless you book a tented camp or a trip that supplies one. Confirm current campsite fees, facilities and booking rules with Kenya Wildlife Service before you travel.

Final Thoughts

The best camping gear in Nairobi is the kit that matches Kenya's cold nights and sudden rain: a waterproof double-wall tent, a sleeping bag rated for your altitude, an insulated pad, a reliable screw-on gas stove and a good headlamp. Buy the sleep system first and check every item before you pay.
